query: How does kube-proxy generate iptables rules to route traffic to a Service's backend pods?

matches.reason: This is the core function that regenerates all kube-proxy NAT-table iptables chains and rules (KUBE-SERVICES/KUBE-SVC/KUBE-SEP) for every Service, including dispatch to cluster/local endpoint policy chains.
For each reachable endpoint this loop creates a KUBE-SEP-* chain and appends the DNAT rule ('-j DNAT --to-destination <podIP:port>') that actually routes matched packets to the backend pod.
Writes the session-affinity and probabilistic load-balancing rules (iptables statistic module with decreasing --probability) that select which backend endpoint chain a Service's traffic jumps to.
